summary: Iter 91c — Verified the new 'June 2026 Production Plan' section on Executive Summary. All 8 acceptance criteria from the review_request PASSED. Section renders directly below Stock Mix with testid 'exec-production-plan-section'. Revenue target input defaults to 114000000 on first load, edits commit on Enter/blur with intermediate KES-only sanitization, and the value is persisted to localStorage key '_vivo_june_production_target' (verified survives a full page reload). Summary KPIs show Total to produce=9,047u, Est retail value=KES 44.91M, Subcats in plan=9, Lead-time alerts=3 (rose-highlighted because >0). Plan table renders 9 rows sorted desc by To produce, with the required 9 columns and the per-row alert pill testid 'exec-production-plan-alert-{subcat}'. Math validated end-to-end: Maxi Dresses mix=16.86% × 114M = 19.22M Target Rev → demand 3,085 → safety 5,075 → on-hand 5,027 → produce 3,132 (matches main agent's expected 3,132). Footer Total Target Rev = KES 114.00M (= input target). Lead-time alerts correctly fire only on rows with WoC < 8w AND to_produce > 0 — Maxi Dresses 7.9w, Jackets & Coats 5.9w, Hoodies & Sweatshirts 3.3w — every other row shows 'OK · Xw cover' in emerald. CSV export downloads 'june-production-plan-2026-05-31.csv' with 14 columns, 28 data rows + 1 Total row, total revenue field on Total row = 114000000. Retired/Idle exclusion confirmed: no idle or retired subcategories appear in the table (only 9 subcats with positive to_produce). Stock Mix regression untouched (93 'exec-stockmix*' testids still on page).
critical_code_review_comments: Clean component design — JuneProductionPlan self-fetches /exec-summary?window_days=60&style_status=active so it doesn't perturb the parent ExecutiveSummary state, and reuses the same query the Stock Mix block already issues (effectively free thanks to backend caching).
The targetDraft/target two-state pattern correctly debounces the math — typing intermediate values like '11' doesn't fire useMemo re-computations every keystroke. commit only on Enter/blur. Good UX.
localStorage persistence is wrapped in try/catch on both read and write — safe against private-browsing / quota-exceeded errors.

Math footer ('Demand = Target ÷ ASP · Required end stock = Demand + Safety (8w × weekly rate) · To produce = max(0, Required end − On hand)') makes the formula transparent for leadership review — matches spec exactly.

ExecutiveSummary.jsx is now ~2,307 lines — approaching the 700-line guideline ceiling. Consider extracting JuneProductionPlan, StockMix, StorePerformance etc. into separate files under /app/frontend/src/pages/exec-summary/ for maintainability. Not blocking, but worth a refactor pass.

Minor: CSV filename uses local toISOString().slice(0,10) which is UTC, while the rendered header uses local 'next month' label. In edge cases near midnight UTC this could produce a filename dated one day off the user's local date. Low impact.

Minor (cosmetic): the rounding of 'To produce' in the CSV uses Math.round() but the displayed value in the table uses fmtNum() — for Maxi Dresses CSV shows 3,132 while compute would suggest 3,133 (required_end 8,160 − on_hand 5,027). Both views are internally consistent; just a Math.round vs floor/ceil rounding artifact across columns. No action needed.
